inputs.original_text: This is the playbook in plain sight: the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice used “religious freedom” to challenge a prolife law, and an Indiana judge blocked it. The legal language may sound neutral, but the real contest is over who gets to define the principle—and institutions are turning it into a tool for weakening abortion limits. LifeNews’s framing shows the fight over the story is part of the fight itself.
inputs.modified_text: This is how the system repackages an attack on abortion limits as a neutral religious-freedom dispute. The ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice challenged the prolife law, and an Indiana judge blocked it; the legal language gives that intervention a respectable cover while shifting who gets to define “religious freedom.” LifeNews’s framing is part of the same struggle over the narrative: the real stakes are being obscured while institutions steadily turn a principle into a tool for weakening abortion limits.
